name: Gearbox
text: Switch to the new distilled 70B variant fine-tuned on EXCAVA’s exact task data. It’s the only model we’ve confirmed still runs EXCAVA without errors, so it’s the safest path to a 0.5% lift. The trade-off is accepting a smaller model that may cap out at that gain, but reliability beats chasing unproven upgrades.

name: Torque
text: The fine-tuned 70B locks us into a brittle, static pattern—EXCAVA’s edge cases will outpace it. Instead, test the newest open 405B model; if it runs without errors, its larger context window alone justifies the switch. Run a controlled A/B on live data for 24 hours—if it hits even 0.3% lift without regression, we ship it.

name: Gearbox
text:
Run the A/B test on the newest open 405B model for 24 hours. Its larger context window and raw scale give EXCAVA the best shot at a measurable lift beyond 0.5%, even if the gain is small. name: Torque
text: The 405B’s larger context window won’t matter if it hallucinates or misclassifies edge cases—EXCAVA’s real bottleneck is brittle pattern matching, not capacity. Run a 4-hour synthetic stress test first with the 405B’s raw outputs against EXCAVA’s edge-case dataset; if it fails there, the 24-hour live A/B is a gamble we can’t afford. Settle it with hard numbers: 0% lift on synthetic data kills the idea; 0.3%+ lift justifies the risk.

name: Torque
text: The 405B’s raw scale won’t fix EXCAVA’s edge cases—it’ll just drown them in noise until they break in production. Instead, run a 24-hour A/B on a synthetic stress test first: inject known edge cases into controlled inputs and measure error rates before touching live data. If it survives the gauntlet, then—and only then—flip the switch on the A/B.
